sections.category: Frontier-lab talent war intensifies as Nobel laureate John Jumper leaves Google DeepMind for Anthropic and Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer departs for OpenAI, set against OpenAI's first look at 2026 cash burn

bullets.body: Two high-profile departures from Google landed in the same 48-hour window. On June 19 John Jumper, who led the AlphaFold team at Google DeepMind for nearly nine years and shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis for that work, announced on X that he is leaving to join Anthropic; Hassabis publicly acknowledged the move and their "extraordinary partnership." It follows by a day the June 18 disclosure that Noam Shazeer, a Google vice president of engineering and co-lead of the Gemini models, is leaving for OpenAI less than two years after Google reportedly paid around 2.7 billion dollars to bring him and his team back from Character.AI; Shazeer is a co-author of the 2017 "Attention Is All You Need" paper that introduced the Transformer architecture underpinning essentially every current frontier model, and Sam Altman welcomed the hire personally. Reporting frames both exits as part of a broader migration of senior research talent away from Google as competitive pressure mounts ahead of its next Gemini release. The backdrop on the financial side is OpenAI's own numbers: investor documents reported June 16 show the company burned about 3.7 billion dollars in the first quarter of 2026 against 5.7 billion in revenue (both roughly triple the year-ago quarter), while ending the period with more than 73 billion dollars in cash and securities after its record spring raise, which on the reported trajectory would let it avoid a near-term round. sections.category: Small-model reasoning: WeiboAI ships VibeThinker-3B, a 3-billion-parameter MIT-licensed model that pushes verifiable math and coding reasoning into a size that runs almost anywhere

bullets.body: WeiboAI (the AI group at Chinese social platform Weibo) released VibeThinker-3B, a dense 3-billion-parameter reasoning model built on Qwen2.5-3B and distributed on Hugging Face under an unrestricted MIT license, with an accompanying paper posted to arXiv (2606.16140) and the surrounding coverage landing June 19. The work is positioned as a study of how far verifiable reasoning can be pushed in a strictly small model: rather than scale parameters, it applies an upgraded "Spectrum-to-Signal" post-training pipeline that first uses curriculum supervised fine-tuning to build a broad spectrum of valid reasoning trajectories, then uses multi-domain reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (plus offline self-distillation and instruction-oriented RL) to amplify the correct ones. The reported results are unusually strong for the size class: roughly 76 on AIME (rising into the 80s with claim-level test-time scaling), about 80 Pass@1 on LiveCodeBench v6, and a 96.1 percent first-attempt acceptance rate on recent unseen LeetCode contests, which the authors offer as evidence of out-of-distribution generalization rather than benchmark memorization. As always with a single-team release the figures are self-reported and await independent reproduction, and there is some inconsistency between the model card's headline numbers and higher figures quoted in secondary coverage; the durable point is that a permissively licensed 3B model now claims competitive verifiable-reasoning scores, which matters most for cheap local and on-device inference. sections.category: Physical AI: Hyundai moves to take full ownership of Boston Dynamics, buying out SoftBank's remaining stake for $325 million

bullets.body: Hyundai Motor Group is moving to take 100 percent ownership of Boston Dynamics, agreeing to buy SoftBank's remaining 9.65 percent stake for about 325 million dollars, according to a June 19 report in South Korea's Maeil Business Newspaper; Hyundai's board is expected to convene on June 22 to approve the purchase. SoftBank is exercising a put option it retained when it sold its controlling position to Hyundai, which paid roughly 880 million dollars for an 80 percent stake in the 2021 deal that valued the company near 1.1 billion dollars. Folding the robotics maker fully into the automaker comes as Boston Dynamics pushes its electric Atlas humanoid from demonstrations into paid industrial deployments, and it concentrates control of one of the most recognizable names in the field at a single strategic owner with both manufacturing scale and a captive set of factory use-cases. The move is a different flavor of the capital now flowing into humanoids than the venture megarounds elsewhere in the sector: instead of an outside syndicate funding a standalone startup, an incumbent industrial parent is consolidating a robotics asset it already largely controls, a signal that strategic owners increasingly see embodied AI as core rather than a financial holding. sections.category: US export controls on Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 draw a bipartisan congressional demand for answers, with the models still offline

bullets.body: The export-control freeze on Anthropic's newest models moved into a congressional-oversight phase. After the Commerce Department's mid-June directive subjecting Fable 5 and Mythos 5 to export controls for all foreign persons (which prompted Anthropic to disable both systems for every customer), a bipartisan group of House members on June 18 formally pressed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to explain the legal basis and the national-security rationale for the action. The new state change is that the dispute now has named legislators on the record demanding documentation, rather than just the company and the administration trading statements: Anthropic maintains the order rests on verbal evidence of a narrow, non-universal jailbreak and notes comparable capabilities exist in competing systems, a reading echoed by security researchers who argue the cited capability (reading a codebase to find and fix flaws) is ordinary defensive security work. Separately, reporting around the G7 indicated President Trump signaled warmer relations with Anthropic following exchanges with chief executive Dario Amodei, hinting at a possible path back, but as of June 19 both models remain offline globally while the company works toward compliance and access has not been restored. The episode is increasingly treated as a precedent-setting test of whether the US will gate frontier models the way it gates advanced chips. sections.category: AI events to plan around now: the next week brings the confidential-computing and offensive-security tracks, then the AI Engineer World's Fair, with the chip and security calendar stretching into the fall

bullets.body: The forward calendar across all three sub-tracks, with the soonest events now only days out. Mainstream dev/data: Snowflake runs a virtual Dev Day on June 25 (two luminary talks plus a hands-on agentic-AI lab); the AI Engineer World's Fair takes over Moscone West with main programming June 29 through July 2 (an optional New Engineer Orientation on June 28), billed as the largest technical AI-engineering conference with over 20 tracks, around 250 speakers, dedicated Inference and Security tracks, and OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Amazon AGI Labs and Microsoft on the floor, preceded by the official AIE World's Fair Hackathon with Cerebral Valley on June 27-28; further out, GitHub Universe returns October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent runs November 30 through December 4 in Las Vegas. AI-security: the Confidential Computing Summit lands June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint (Linux Foundation and OPAQUE, with confidential-AI and data-sovereignty keynotes featuring AMD, Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Meta, Samsung and others); AI Tinkerers San Francisco hosts an Offensive Security Demo Night on June 25 with live autonomous-pentesting-agent demos (sponsor XBOW); SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit follows August 11-12 at Half Moon Bay; Black Hat USA's AI Summit runs August 1-6 in Las Vegas alongside DEF CON's AI Village; and OWASP Global AppSec USA is November 5-6 in San Francisco. Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series remains on the watch list. AI-chip/hardware: AMD's Advancing AI 2026 is set for July 23 at Moscone (Instinct MI400-series focus expected); Hot Chips 2026 runs August 23-25 at Stanford; and the AI Infra Summit is September 15-17 at the Santa Clara Convention Center.
